title: Add Chart.js as an independent core bundle with a PrestaShop palette for the Symfony dashboard
issue_body:
# Spike: Chart library benchmark (replace D3 v3 + NVD3)

**Context.** The dashboard relies on D3 v3 and NVD3, both unmaintained (NVD3 is effectively abandoned and pins D3 v3). The goal of this spike is to identify a stable, widely-adopted replacement — the library choice is the outcome of the spike, not a given.

## Hard constraints (any candidate must satisfy)

- **Framework fit:** works with the BO stack — Symfony/Twig + vanilla JS. No dependency on a specific frontend framework (e.g. React-only libraries don't fit our rendering model).
- **License:** compatible with OSS *and* commercial distribution to merchants. Watch for "free under revenue threshold" or attribution-required terms — those are potential blockers to confirm with legal.
- **Maintenance:** actively maintained, recent releases, healthy issue turnaround. This is the core reason we're moving off NVD3.
- **Chart coverage:** covers the chart types actually used on the dashboard (line, bar, pie/doughnut, area at minimum).

**Advices:** In PrestaShop SA some teams use chart in their module. Discuss with them to check if we could reuse the same library.

## Evaluation grid (to fill per candidate)

| Criteria | What to look at |
|---|---|
| Adoption / stability | npm weekly downloads, GitHub stars, release cadence, last commit |
| License | exact terms, commercial-use compatibility |
| Bundle size | gzipped core + tree-shaking support |
| Rendering | Canvas / SVG, performance on our data volumes |
| Integration effort | data feed from BO controllers, theming vs BO design tokens |
| Accessibility | ARIA support out of the box or via plugin |
| DX & docs | API clarity, TypeScript support, examples |

## Method

1. Fill the grid above for each candidate identified.
2. Shortlist the top 1–2 against our constraints.

## Expected deliverable

The filled evaluation grid + a documented recommendation with rationale, and the PoC branch/screenshot by solution choosen. Make an example module by solution.

title: Migrate Dashboard to Symfony behind a beta feature flag (initialization)
issue_body:
## Context

The admin Dashboard is the last fully legacy entry-point page of the Back Office: legacy `AdminDashboardController`, Smarty templates from the default admin theme, legacy `addJS()` asset loading, and content provided by native modules (`dashactivity`, `dashtrends`, `dashgoals`, `dashproducts`) through legacy hooks (`dashboardZoneOne/Two/Three`, `dashboardData`, `displayDashboardTop`, `displayDashboardToolbarTopMenu`).

The spike #41522 analyzed the page and confirmed the migration is feasible. Following the maintainers' review of the spike, a structural decision was made that shapes this epic:

> **No Smarty / legacy `Helper*` retro-compatibility on the Symfony page.** The new page must not initialize Smarty template dirs, must not shim the legacy controller for `get_class()` checks, and must not attempt to render legacy module hook output. Instead, the Symfony Dashboard dispatches **new dedicated hooks**, so a module knows which architecture it is integrating with purely from which hook is called — no version/context detection needed on the module side. Modules can register on both hook families to stay compatible across PrestaShop versions.

As a consequence, the native `dash*` modules will **not** display anything on the new page until they are migrated (subsequent stories). This is why the new page is gated behind a feature flag (beta), following the same pattern as previous feature-flag-gated migrated pages (e.g. Countries).

This story delivers the foundation: feature flag, Symfony controller, routing, Twig layout dispatching the new hooks, and an example module demonstrating and validating the new integration contract.

## User story

> **As a** module developer / merchant on the beta channel,
> **I want** the Back Office Dashboard to run on a Symfony controller rendering a Twig layout that exposes new dedicated hooks,
> **so that** modules can integrate with the modern Dashboard through an explicit, unambiguous contract, without any dependency on Smarty or legacy Helper classes.

## Scope

### 1. Feature flag

- Add a new feature flag `dashboard` (constant `FeatureFlagSettings::FEATURE_FLAG_DASHBOARD`), stability **beta**, disabled by default.
- Declare it in the feature flag fixtures/install data so it appears in **Advanced Parameters > New & Experimental Features**, with proper label and description (wording: "Dashboard page" + mention that native dashboard modules are not yet compatible with the new page).
- Behaviour:
  - **Flag OFF (default):** the legacy `AdminDashboardController` keeps working exactly as today. Zero change for merchants and modules.
  - **Flag ON:** accessing the Dashboard (menu entry, `getAdminLink('AdminDashboard')`, direct legacy URL) serves the new Symfony page. The legacy controller redirects to the Symfony route when the flag is enabled, following the redirection mechanism already used by other feature-flag-gated migrated pages.
- Add the upgrade SQL entry so the flag is created on shops upgrading to the target version.

### 2. Symfony controller

- Create `src/PrestaShopBundle/Controller/Admin/DashboardController.php` extending `PrestaShopAdminController`.
- Actions in this story:
  - `indexAction(Request $request)`: resolves the employee date range (`date_from` / `date_to`, reusing the existing per-employee stats date configuration), dispatches the new display hooks (see §4), renders the Twig layout.
- Explicitly **not** in this controller (per the spike review decision):
  - no `AdminDashboardController` shim instantiation, no `Context->controller` override;
  - no `Hook::exec('actionAdminControllerSetMedia')` for legacy module asset injection;
  - no `smarty->addTemplateDir(...)` setup;
  - no port of the legacy AJAX actions (`refreshDashboard`, `setSimulationMode`, `saveDashConfig`) — the data-refresh contract will be redesigned with the new JS architecture in a dedicated story.
- Security: standard `AdminSecurity` attribute with the same permission profile as the legacy page (`AdminDashboard` tab).

### 3. Routing

- Create `src/PrestaShopBundle/Resources/config/routing/admin/dashboard.yml`:

```yaml
admin_dashboard_index:
  path: /
  methods: [ GET ]
  defaults:
    _controller: 'PrestaShopBundle\Controller\Admin\DashboardController::indexAction'
    _legacy_controller: AdminDashboard
    _legacy_link: AdminDashboard
  options:
    expose: true
```

- Register the resource in the admin routing aggregator (`admin.yml`) under the `/dashboard` prefix.
- `getAdminLink('AdminDashboard')` must resolve to the Symfony route when the feature flag is enabled (via `_legacy_link`), and to the legacy URL otherwise.

### 4. Twig template + new dedicated hooks

- Create `src/PrestaShopBundle/Resources/views/Admin/Dashboard/index.html.twig` porting the layout structure of `view.tpl` (three-zone layout: Zone One / Zone Two / Zone Three), based on the standard admin layout — **without** porting `HelperCalendar`, the legacy toolbar hooks, or the legacy JS stack.
- Define and dispatch a new hook family, distinct from every existing legacy hook name to avoid any collision or ambiguity:

| New hook | Type | Dispatched from | Parameters | Legacy counterpart |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `displayAdminDashboardZoneOne` | display | `indexAction` | `date_from`, `date_to` | `dashboardZoneOne` |
| `displayAdminDashboardZoneTwo` | display | `indexAction` | `date_from`, `date_to` | `dashboardZoneTwo` |
| `displayAdminDashboardZoneThree` | display | `indexAction` | `date_from`, `date_to` | `dashboardZoneThree` |
| `displayAdminDashboardTop` | display | Twig layout | `date_from`, `date_to` | `displayDashboardTop` |
| `displayAdminDashboardToolbar` | display | Twig layout | — | `displayDashboardToolbarTopMenu` |

> Naming to be validated with maintainers before implementation; the constraint is: `display` prefix (PrestaShop display-hook convention), a namespace that cannot be confused with the legacy family, and symmetry across zones. The legacy hooks are untouched and keep working on the legacy page.

- Hook output contract: hooks return HTML strings, injected with `|raw` in the corresponding zone blocks. Modules are expected to render their own templates (Twig recommended) and manage their own assets; the core page makes **no assumption** about module internals (no Smarty dirs, no Helper classes, no controller class-name check).
- Register the new hooks in the official hook definitions (install XML data + upgrade entry) with descriptions, so they are documented and discoverable (hook reference in devdocs to be updated — see DoD).
- Empty-state: when a zone receives no content (which will be the nominal case in beta until `dash*` modules are migrated), display a clean placeholder (empty-state component) rather than a blank column.

### 5. Example module

- Create a `dashexample` module (target: `PrestaShop/example-modules` repository) that serves both as living documentation of the new contract and as a validation vehicle:
  - registers `displayAdminDashboardZoneOne`, `displayAdminDashboardZoneTwo` and `displayAdminDashboardToolbar`;
  - renders its content through module Twig templates (no Smarty, no `HelperForm`, no `Db::getInstance()` — a static or trivially computed content is enough);
  - loads its own CSS/JS assets from its hook output or via standard module asset registration, without relying on `actionAdminControllerSetMedia` + controller class-name detection;
  - includes a README section explaining the legacy-vs-Symfony hook families and how a module can register on both to support multiple PrestaShop versions.
- The module is used to manually validate (and later automate) that hook dispatch, parameter passing and HTML injection work end to end.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Flag OFF:** the legacy Dashboard is strictly unchanged — legacy controller, Smarty templates, legacy hooks, `dash*` widgets and AJAX refresh all work as before.
2. **Flag ON:**
   - opening the Dashboard from the BO menu or via `getAdminLink('AdminDashboard')` lands on the Symfony page (URL under the Symfony admin routing, valid security token);
   - a direct hit on the legacy Dashboard URL redirects to the Symfony route;
   - the page renders the three-zone layout with empty-state placeholders and no PHP error/warning in logs;
   - no Smarty template dir registration and no legacy `Helper*` class is involved in the rendering path (verified by code review);
   - submitting the date range persists the employee configuration and the page reflects the new range.
3. **Hooks:**
   - the five new hooks exist in the `hook` table after fresh install **and** after upgrade;
   - with `dashexample` installed and the flag ON, its content appears in Zone One, Zone Two and the toolbar area
   - with `dashexample` installed and the flag OFF, the legacy page is unaffected (module registers only the new hooks);
   - none of the new hook names collides with an existing hook (legacy Dashboard hooks included).
4. **Non-regression:** existing legacy Dashboard behaviour is covered by the current test status quo; no existing UI/integration test regresses with the flag OFF.

## Out of scope (subsequent stories)

- New data-refresh contract replacing `hookDashboardData` + `dashboard.js` AJAX (design of the modern equivalent, likely typed payloads + a dedicated action hook family).
- JS stack modernisation (webpack entry point, replacement of D3 v3 / NVD3).
- Migration of the native `dash*` modules to the new hooks (per-module stories, parallelisable).
- Demo/simulation mode (`PS_DASHBOARD_SIMULATION`) on the new page.
- Removal of the legacy controller and legacy hook dispatch (final cleanup, once modules are migrated and the flag is promoted to stable).

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Feature flag created (install fixtures + upgrade SQL), visible in New & Experimental Features, default OFF
- [ ] `DashboardController` + routing merged, `_legacy_link` mapping verified
- [ ] Twig layout merged, new hooks dispatched and registered (install + upgrade)
- [ ] `dashexample` module published in `example-modules` with README
- [ ] Manual QA scenario executed (flag OFF/ON matrix, with and without `dashexample`)
- [ ] Devdocs updated: new hooks documented in the hook reference + migration note for module developers (legacy vs Symfony dashboard integration)
- [ ] Spike #41522 linked; epic issue references this story as prerequisite for all following stories

## References

- Spike: PrestaShop/PrestaShop#41522 (analysis + maintainer review comments)
- Legacy controller: `controllers/admin/AdminDashboardController.php`
- Legacy view: `admin-dev/themes/default/template/controllers/dashboard/helpers/view/view.tpl`
- Native modules impacted (later stories): `dashactivity`, `dashtrends`, `dashgoals`, `dashproducts`

issue_title: [Extra Properties] The translation scanner must detect the extra property
issue_body:
As a PrestaShop user, I want to translate the extra properties label and description from the BO in the Translations section

## Problem

When we register an extra property we can define its label and descriptions:

```php
$productDangerousRegistered = $this->registerExtraProperty(
            new ExtraPropertyDefinition(
                entityName: 'product',
                propertyName: 'is_dangerous',
                type: ExtraPropertyType::BOOL,
                scope: ExtraPropertyScope::COMMON,
                defaultValue: 0,
                nullable: false,
                displayApi: true,
                associatedForms: ['product:options.suppliers:before'],
                associatedGrids: ['product:reference'],
                formFieldType: SwitchType::class,
                validator: 'isBool',
                labelWording: 'Dangerous product',
                labelDomain: self::TRANSLATION_DOMAIN,
                descriptionWording: 'Indicates whether the product is dangerous',
                descriptionDomain: self::TRANSLATION_DOMAIN,
            )
        );
```

The problem is that since we don't use `trans` nor `l` we don't scan these new wordings so they do not appear in the translation BO interface if we want to edit their translation.

## Solution

We need to improve the TranslationBundle responsible for scanning the code to find translations; it should be able to scan `ExtraPropertyDefinition` from modules and add them into the catalogue.

Two approaches for this:
- code approach: we scan the module's code and search for `ExtraPropertyDefinition` class creation, then we extract the fields and add the workdings to the module catalog
- (recommended) DB approach we fetch the definitions in the DB and update the catalog based on the wording we found, I'd recommend this approach because it's easier to scan a DB rather than code, if a definition is removed from DB so are its related translations And when we add the dynamic _core definitions it will work out of the box (if we don't no code can be scanned when the definition ahs been added from the BO)

title: Discount priority system
issue_title: Making priorities for discounts (if apply automatically)
issue_body:
# Context
Discounts can be compatible with each other. This means that a customer can benefit from multiple discounts at the same time (they are combined) if their order meets the trigger conditions for those discounts.


Only discounts at the product level, cart level, and order level can be compatible with others of the same type. However, all discount types can be compatible with other types.

When multiple compatible discounts apply to the same order, they must follow a specific order of application:
1. The "priority" field is used to define the order
2. If this field is not filled in or if multiple discounts have the same priority value, the order is determined by the discount type (1 - Catalog, 2 - Cart,  3 - Shipping, 4 - Free gift)
3. If at least two discounts of the same type share the same priority, they are then sorted based on their creation date

In cases where multiple discounts exist but are all mutually incompatible, the same rules are used to determine which discount should be applied.

The calculation base for a discount is the result of the order amount after applying all higher-priority discounts.

Each time a discount is applied, the list of eligible and compatible discounts is regenerated in the correct order of application.

Regarding the `priority` field, it is still available in the cart rule entity but can no longer be edit via the BO UI

# Tests
##  Order
**GIVEN:** a discount with a priority equal to 1 compatible with a discount of priority equal to 2
**WHEN:** the discounts are applied automaticaly
**THEN:** the first discount is applied then the second discount is applied (only if its trigger conditions correspond to the new discounted order amount)

**GIVEN:** a discount with a priority equal to 1 incompatible with a discount of priority equal to 2
**WHEN:** the discounts are applied automaticaly
**THEN:** only the first discount is applied

- [x] If a valid customer is selected → discount creation succeeds ✅

title: Filter experimental apis
issue_title: Hide Endpoint on the endpoint list when the endpoint is not fully finished
issue_body:
### Issue

For an endpoint to be considered fully completed, it needs to be tested, documented, and accessible in the interface. The issue arises when some endpoints are still a work in progress during a release, causing delays in development. Committers are then required to either complete the pending work or backport it.

### Solutions

To streamline the development and contribution process, it would be beneficial to hide the experimental/work-in-progress endpoints.

### Specs

Implement a feature flag for endpoints; when an endpoint is marked as experimental,

If the feature flag is disabled, the experimental endpoints will not be accessible.

Endpoints won't be display on the doc swagger

If all the endpoints from one scope are experimental, then hide the scope on the API Client form

### Acceptance test

When an endpoint is marked as experimental...

### Technical solution

Add a parameter on our CQRS operations:

```php
#[ApiResource(
    operations: [
        new CQRSUpdate(
            uriTemplate: '/cart-rule',
            CQRSCommand: EditCartRuleCommand::class,
            // This is optional and false by default
            experimental: true,
        ),
    ],
)]
```

When the experimental config is true endpoint is not visible in prod nor in dev
Add a feature flag `Show hidden API endpoints` to ignore this config, then the endpoints become visible in both prod and dev
Scopes that are assigned ONLY to experimental endpoints should be filtered out
To implement this feature we need to override/decorate the scanning mechanism of ApiPlatform and filter some operations (hint look into the `ResourceMetadataCollectionFactoryInterface` that was already decorated)

Hint:
Look into this old decorator https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/b2dbfdeddff99112b68d0744606fe87d1f6d670c/src/PrestaShopBundle/ApiPlatform/Metadata/ScopesToSecurityMetadataCollectionFactoryDecorator.php The principle should be similar but instead of adding some extra properties we remove the operation from the collection
